removability.rationale: Dropping a feature means deleting its route plus scattered-but-guessable edits in functions.ts, pokeapi.ts, the Pokémon page and a CSS rule; TypeScript won't flag the orphaned server exports, so dead code is easy to leave but trivial to grep.

changeability.rationale: Nearly every cross-cutting rule (card markup, card data normalization, sprite URLs, humanized names, titles, em-dash, sorting) has exactly one obvious home, so the classic 'fix it in every list' bug class is designed out.

coupling.rationale: Clean server/client separation with narrow interfaces and explicit seams; the one tangle is reaching into the router's private _notFound match flag for the 404 title, which is upgrade-fragile.

app/src/components/TypeBadge.tsx:5 — link boolean flag is the only flag-creep in sight
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared pieces stretch to real variation (extra callback, optional props, config tables) with almost no flag parameters; the residual cost is ~10 lines of per-route loader/head boilerplate duplicated four times, which is idiomatic for file-based routing.

findings.issue: Root head() reads the router's internal `m._notFound` field (underscore-private) to set the 404 title, which can break silently on router upgrades.
findings.suggestion: Rely on documented state only (m.status === 'notFound'), or have the shared NotFound route component contribute the title via a route-level head, keeping internals out of user code.

findings.issue: The missing-value '—' rule is implemented twice: server fns bake EM_DASH into effect fields (functions.ts:130,142) while the client renders numbers/stats via display() (app/src/lib/format.ts:23).
findings.suggestion: Return null from the server DTO and let the single display() helper own the em dash everywhere.

findings.issue: The loader → serverFn → null-check → notFound() + head block is duplicated verbatim in all four detail routes.
findings.suggestion: A tiny per-route helper (or a shared makeDetailRoute pattern) would keep future pages like Items to one-liner wiring; acceptable as-is given file-based routing conventions.

findings.issue: Search-as-you-type is implemented with dual state (query + lastPushed ref) and two interacting effects with subtle equality guards, the hardest-to-change code in the app.
findings.suggestion: Extract the debounced-search/URL-sync into a small useDebouncedSearch hook so the page just renders, and the behavior is testable in isolation.

findings.issue: All resources (species, types, generations, moves, abilities, evolution) live in one growing module separated only by comment banners; at this scale fine, but an Items addition makes it six.
findings.suggestion: If it keeps growing, split pokeapi.ts per resource, keeping the memo cache in its own module shared by each.

findings.issue: .card-note (the ability-page-only 'Hidden ability' label) is feature-specific CSS in the global stylesheet, so feature removal leaves dead rules behind.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given plain-CSS-without-framework constraint; note it in the removal checklist.

summary: A well-layered, current-idiom TanStack Start app: server-only data access with caching in one module, view DTOs across a clean RPC boundary, and one shared component per cross-cutting concern so most fixes land in one obvious place. Feature removal requires a handful of findable edits across route, server functions, data module and CSS rather than a single delete. The only real weaknesses are a peek at router internals for the 404 title and small boilerplate duplication across the four detail routes.
